overall: The AG resolved the complaint by informal action and found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law, because the law does not bar members from disclosing executive session topics and G.L. c. 30A, § 22(e) does not apply.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a selectman shared executive session notes and confidential information about a job applicant with a group outside the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, the law does not require that public body members keep topics discussed in executive session confidential nor does it impose penalties for members' failure to do so.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued that G.L. c. 30A, § 22(e) required confidentiality of the documents at issue.
allegations.key_passage: As this section concerns only documents used at an open session meeting, we find it is inapplicable to the present situation, which concerns documents allegedly used during an executive session discussion.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes did not identify which statutory purpose justified the closed session; AG issued a reminder rather than a finding.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes of the Board's December 2, 2014 executive session do not identify which of the ten permissible purposes for executive session the Board invoked to justify the executive session, as required by G.L. c. 30A, § 21(b)(3).

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
